newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, LSFO softer.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, LSFO softer.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Wednesday, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil markets were steady and quiet although dealers felt that trader bids were above levels that supply and demand would normally dictate.
Low sulphur markets were quiet, too, and prices were a little softer despite a strengthening crude oil market because supply was seen good. Swaps eased back to around $94.50 a tonne fob NWE
Up to three prompt low sulphur cargoes were seen available in NWE and offers were pegged up at $96 fob NWE.
In the Med, Russian heating oil was seen offered at premiums of between $3 and $3.50 over cif high Med quotes basis Genoa and bid at between $1.50 and $2.25 over.
Outright prices rose $2 a tonne with IPE futures. Discussion was slow. "There's not much buying and not much material either,' said one trader.

Syria agreed to buy a total of 100,000 tonnes of 0.7 percent sulphur gas oil at premiums of around $9.50 to $9.75 above the fob Med mean quotations from German trader Stinnes and Swiss trader Onyx Oil, traders said.
Although no fresh naphtha Med cargo deals were heard done and the arb to Asia remained closed, brokers referred to interest in Med volumes to Brazil as Egyptian FOB stems were heard available.

The Turkish monthly tender was heard awarded late Tuesday or early Wednesday, but the result was not widely known. In general, fairly widespread buying interest was seen in the Med in the context of poor supply.
